sources.text:
Monfragüe is a comarca in Extremadura, western Spain, and the site of Monfragüe National Park. The national park lies in the province of Cáceres, roughly between Plasencia, Trujillo, and the city of Cáceres. It covers 18,118 hectares (181.18 km2) and extends along the valley of the Tagus River, where the Tiétar River joins it. Its habitats include extensive scrubland, oak woodland, cliffs, and rocky outcrops.
The area was declared a natural park in 1979, recognised by UNESCO as a biosphere reserve in 2003, and designated a Spanish national park in 2007. It is particularly noted for its birdlife and is protected as a Special Protection Area for birds. Monfragüe is an important breeding area for raptors, including cinereous vultures, griffon vultures, and Spanish imperial eagles, and also supports species such as black storks, deer, wild boar, and reintroduced Iberian lynx.


== Location ==
Monfragüe is a comarca in Spain, i.e. a county, with no administrative role in Extremadura, western Spain.
